title: Water
keywords: water stream well rain barrel boil contamination treatment
text:
1. Prefer sealed drinking water.
2. Fuel, chemicals or floodwater suspected? Find another source. Boiling does not remove those contaminants.
3. For germ risk: settle cloudy water, filter through a clean cloth, then bring to a rolling boil for 1 minute; 3 minutes above 6,500 feet. Cool in a clean, covered container.
4. Treatment tablets: follow that product’s label.
A clear stream or mapped well is not proof of safe water.
question: What source is the water from, and could fuel, chemicals or floodwater have reached it?

title: Food after a power cut
keywords: food refrigerator fridge freezer eat milk meat power outage smell
text:
1. Keep fridge and freezer doors closed.
2. Without power or another cold source: a fridge keeps food cold for about 4 hours; a full freezer about 48 hours, half-full about 24.
3. Discard refrigerated perishables after 4 hours without cooling. Never taste food to test safety.
4. Frozen food can be refrozen if it still has ice crystals or is 40°F or colder.
Use measured temperature and elapsed time, not smell.
question: What food is it, how long was cooling lost, and do you have a temperature reading?

title: Toilets without water
keywords: toilet toilets sanitation sewage waste running water hygiene bucket handwashing hands soap wash
text:
1. Do not flush if sewage is backing up or the sewer/septic system may be damaged.
2. Use a stable, lidded bucket lined with a heavy plastic bag as a temporary toilet.
3. Keep waste sealed, away from food, children and water sources. Use a designated disposal point when available; never empty it into a drain or stream.
4. Keep soap and safe handwashing water beside the toilet. Assign someone to restock and check it.
Scrub all hand surfaces with soap for 20 seconds, then rinse and dry.

title: Check a building
keywords: building shelter stay house gas leak fire flood cracks damage evacuation
text:
Leave if you smell gas, see fire, hear structural movement, or see major leaning or collapse. Move clear of power lines and floodwater.
Do not operate switches or make flames where gas may be leaking.
Do not enter a damaged building until a qualified person has checked it. A photo or description cannot establish structural safety.
From outside, record the damage, location and time in Plan → Log.
question: What damage or warning signs can you see from a safe place?

title: Read an equipment warning
keywords: equipment warning fault code generator inverter manual model troubleshooting
text:
1. Write down the exact brand, model and warning code.
2. Add its manual in Docs, or paste the warning text into Chat.
3. Ask Jarvis to find that code in that manual and explain the listed checks.
4. Stop using equipment that is smoking, leaking, sparking or overheating. Follow the manual’s shutdown procedure if safe.
A code from a different model may mean something else. Do not bypass a protection device.
Run generators outdoors, at least 20 feet from doors, windows and vents.
question: What is the exact model and warning code?

title: Check power parts
keywords: solar panel battery batteries charger cable voltage volts amps compatibility compatible parts inverter
text:
Copy the labels and manuals for every part before connecting anything.
Check battery chemistry and voltage; charger battery settings; panel open-circuit voltage, including cold-weather rise; controller input limits; and cable, connector and fuse ratings.
Every limit must match the actual equipment and configuration. A matching plug alone proves nothing.
Jarvis can compare supplied ratings. Missing ratings mean compatibility is not established.

title: Fix something
keywords: fix repair bicycle bike tire pump filter broken tools parts
text:
1. Name the item, exact model, symptom and tools you have.
2. Add its manual in Docs. Ask for one check at a time.
3. Isolate its energy or pressure as its manual requires before work.
For a bicycle puncture: locate the leak and the object that caused it; use the correct tube patch or replacement tube. Follow the patch maker’s instructions. Check tire seating and brakes before riding.
For a drinking-water filter, use its approved parts and cleaning method; a repair does not prove filtration performance.

title: Plant and grow
keywords: grow planting garden seeds crop harvest frost soil vegetables calendar
text:
1. List your seeds in Plan → Garden.
2. Check each seed packet for temperature, depth, spacing, light and time to harvest.
3. Use your local frost history, soil temperature and current observations. A date for another state is not your planting date.
4. Add a regional growing guide in Docs. Save your planting date and next check in Garden.
Record watering, damage and harvests. The calculated harvest date is an estimate from your packet, not a promise.

title: Preserve food
keywords: preserve preservation canning canned pressure canner recipe jars harvest shelf storage low acid
text:
Use a tested recipe from USDA or the National Center for Home Food Preservation.
Match the exact food, preparation, jar size, processing method and elevation adjustment. Do not invent shorter times or ingredient substitutions.
Low-acid foods need an appropriate pressure-canning process. A pressure cooker is not automatically a suitable pressure canner.
Add the exact recipe to Docs before starting. If the recipe or required equipment is missing, choose another storage method.
question: What food, tested recipe and preserving equipment do you have?

title: Find each other
keywords: find each other radio meet meeting communication channel schedule check in
text:
1. Choose a familiar meeting point and a backup. Save them in Plan → People.
2. Agree on check-in times and what to do if someone misses one.
3. For radios, use the same channel and settings; check the actual manual. Test nearby before relying on range.
4. Keep messages short: who, where, need, next check-in.
5. If local Wi-Fi still works, start Plan → Messages. Share its address and code with your group. Internet and satellites are not needed.

title: Choose what comes first
keywords: task priority first daylight daily plan time water energy needs urgent
text:
1. Address immediate danger and urgent care.
2. Check drinking water, shelter, temperature and food.
3. List the work in Plan → Today. Mark Now, Today or Later.
4. Assign one person, a deadline and anything needed first.
5. Use Plan → Supplies and Power to see constraints. Recheck after conditions change.
Plan with observed weather and available daylight; Jarvis has no live forecast.
question: What is the most urgent need, and how much daylight, water and battery power remain?
prompt: Using my saved situation and tasks, what should we do first?

title: Make supplies last
keywords: supply supplies inventory lasts food water fuel medication stock ration amount daily
text:
In Plan → Supplies, enter the amount left, its unit and how much your group uses each day.
Days left = amount left ÷ daily use. Keep both amounts in the same unit.
Update the amount after use, losses or resupply. Estimates do not verify quality or availability.
For medication, record only an existing prescribed schedule. Do not change a dose to make stock last.
Ask Jarvis which recorded supply will run out first.
question: What amount is left, and how much is used per day?
prompt: Using my saved supplies, what will run out first?

title: Budget power
keywords: power budget watts watt-hours wh energy solar charge device battery days
text:
In Plan → Power, list each device’s running watts and hours per day.
Daily energy = watts × hours. Battery watt-hours = volts × amp-hours, before usable-capacity limits and losses.
Enter usable battery energy and a solar estimate based on panel watts, equivalent full-sun hours and charging efficiency.
The app shows daily demand, estimated generation and shortfall. Battery-only days assume no charging.
Keep reserve for essential devices. Nameplate solar output is not guaranteed daily production.
question: What battery capacity and device wattages are shown on the labels?
prompt: Using my saved power budget, how can we keep essentials running longer?

title: First aid basics
keywords: first aid bleeding injured injury medical care wound
text:
Make the scene safe before approaching.
For severe external bleeding, apply firm, steady direct pressure with a dressing or clean cloth; use a barrier against blood if available. Seek reachable trained help.
For other injuries, tell Jarvis what happened, symptoms, age group and available supplies. Use downloaded first-aid references.
Jarvis cannot examine someone, diagnose an injury or choose medication doses. Hands-free answers do not replace practical first-aid training.
question: What happened, and what symptoms can you observe?

title: Work as a group
keywords: community people skills resources responsibility request help rebuild project maintenance dependencies
text:
Use Plan → People for skills, needs, shared supplies and responsibilities.
Use Today for repair projects: name the job, owner, due date, materials needed first and next maintenance check.
Use Log to separate direct observations, reports, assumptions and decisions.
Review unfinished work at a regular check-in. Keep a paper copy of meeting points and essential tasks in case the device loses power.
